A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAG study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched across relocation, including v1 Appendix I becoming v2 Section 4.4.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, role and voting ablations, robustness tests, consistency measurements, deployment costs, and agent-population and backbone comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a derived utility–resource analysis in Appendix C.4 and Table 8.

M1.justification: The four agent roles, hybrid debate workflow, RAG, and GRPO/CTDE optimization remain unchanged. Mixed-backbone SAG was already evaluated in v1 Appendix I; its promotion to Section 4.4 introduces no method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eight benchmarks in Table 1 and retain the demographic counterfactual and linguistic/adversarial perturbation scenarios. Newly discussed emergency and offline clinical workflows are applicability examples, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain the same Llama/Qwen baselines, PPO/DPO variants, Meditron, Me-LLaMA, and role-removal and majority-voting controls. The new efficiency summary uses DPO and GRPO systems already compared in Table 2.

E3.justification: Appendix C.4 adds two evaluation metrics: accuracy per peak GPU memory and inverse Gap per latency. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. The added majority-voting description clarifies an existing control rather than establishing a changed experiment.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a quantitative utility–resource trade-off analysis using derived efficiency ratios. Existing role ablations, population scaling, robustness tests, and case studies are retained. The backbone-diversity analysis is relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions retain standard deviations over five runs in the consistency tables and the ten-run consensus-rate definition in Appendix B.6. No seed, confidence-interval, significance-testing, or repeated-run reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 2 corrects the Qwen PPO Gap from 193 to 19.3. New Table 8 reports derived averages and efficiency values, including APM 0.51 for Llama-DPO versus 1.09 for SAG-Llama-GRPO. Other matched results, including the relocated heterogeneity and scaling tables, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 introduces mathematical definitions for APM as average accuracy divided by memory and RPL as 1/(Gap × latency). The existing optimization formulations and metric equations in Appendices A–B are unchanged; no proof or theorem is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: specialized small-agent collaboration can substitute for parameter scaling and improve clinical utility while trading additional latency and computation for lower memory requirements.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly identifies emergency triage, real-time ICU monitoring, and live assistants as potentially unsuitable because of latency, while identifying case review and second opinions as more appropriate uses. This adds concrete applicability boundaries to the earlier general defense of the latency trade-off.

D1.justification: v2 specifies that majority-voting agents retain specialized roles and aggregate outputs equally without hierarchical coordination. It also removes v1's code-release statement and sole repository link from the introduction, reducing access guidance without establishing that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: Section 5 now acknowledges prior role specialization and distinguishes SAG through clinically grounded separation of reasoning, verification, safety, and adjudication. Citations are added, replaced, or removed, including additions of More et al. (2026) and Wang et al. (2026). Several other changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: v2 moves Appendix I into Section 4.4, locally revises related-work and appendix discussion, adds acknowledgements, and replaces the preprint footer with proceedings information. Most wording and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the utility–resource Table 8 and moves v1's heterogeneity Table 10 into the main text as Table 6. Other tables and Figure 7 undergo relocation or reflow; the seven existing figures and most table formats are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity through concrete latency limitations, a better-described voting control, more qualified research positioning, and the Table 2 correction. However, it removes the sole code-access link. Its new efficiency table also combines optimized accuracies with costs reported for pre-trained SAG in Table 7 without explaining their applicability. With the underlying experiments otherwise unchanged, these benefits and reproducibility uncertainties do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
